notes:
I couldn't write these notes, because my research tool stopped working before I could read any sources. On my first attempt to fetch the Isaiah 44 pages, the system said I had no more tool calls left for this turn. A second attempt was refused the same way. I didn't get to read a single page.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for every point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse notes from memory, because they would break both rules.

**Pages I was about to read:**
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-44/
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/isaiah/44.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/isaiah/44.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/isaiah/44.htm
- Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/isaiah-44-commentary
- NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Isaiah+44

**Verses I planned to look at most closely, each needing a source before it goes in your notes:**
- **v. 3 (God pouring out His Spirit):** how Pentecostal and charismatic teachers (ag.org, samstorms.org) read it, compared with Reformed and Wesleyan writers.
- **v. 18 (whether God closed their eyes):** how Reformed and Wesleyan/Arminian writers handle it, plus what the NET notes say about how to translate it.
- **v. 22 ("I have blotted out… Return to Me"):** how traditions explain the order of God's forgiveness and the call to turn back.
- **vv. 24–28 (Cyrus named in advance):** the modern scholarly view that a later author wrote this part of Isaiah (bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org), compared with the traditional view of one author.
- **v. 6 ("I am the first and I am the last"):** Catholic, Orthodox and church-father readings (newadvent.org, oca.org) that link it to Revelation 1 and 22.

If you ask again in a new message, my tool access should reset. I'll then read these pages and write the notes verse by verse, with a link after every point and anything I can't find left out.
